clinician.final_diagnosis: Cutaneous melanocytic tumor with CRTC1::TRIM11 fusion
clinician.trajectory_summary: An 18-year-old female presented with a 3-year history of a slow-growing dull red mass on her left leg that was occasionally tender. B-ultrasound in July 2022 revealed a hypoechoic nodule measuring 1.2 × 1 cm in the proximal left leg subcutaneous soft tissue with distinct boundary, uneven internal echo, and enhanced posterior echo; no blood flow signal was detected on CDFI, and no lymphadenopathy was noted. A biopsy was performed, revealing a well-circumscribed nodular mass in the dermis composed of nests, fascicles, bundles, or sheets of epithelioid cells with round/oval nuclei, abundant cytoplasm, prominent nucleoli, and visible mitosis, with local nevus cell clusters and a positive basal margin. Immunohistochemistry confirmed melanocytic differentiation with positive staining for S-100, SOX10, Melan-A, and focal HMB-45, with retention of INI1 and H3K27Me3 nuclear expression and a proliferation index of approximately 10%. Next-generation sequencing and fluorescence in situ hybridization confirmed the pathognomonic CRTC1::TRIM11 fusion, establishing the diagnosis of cutaneous melanocytic tumor. Surgical treatment was performed, and six-month postoperative follow-up revealed no local recurrence or metastasis.
